items.title: November 21 | Federal Reserve: Household Inflation Expectations Ease, So Why Does Cook Still Favor a Rate Increase? · Goodman Macro
items.excerpt: On November 20, 2026, Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook explained at the Central Bank of Chile’s annual conference why she had voted for a 25-basis-point rate increase in October. She argued that current interest rates still support strong investment and consumption, and that September’s single rate increase might not be enough to bring inflation down on a sustained basis. A University of Michigan survey released the same day, meanwhile, showed that U.S. households’ inflation expectations for the year ahead fell by 1 percentage point in a single month. Together, these developments pose a practical question for the December ... At its October 28 policy meeting, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) voted 10–2 to maintain the federal funds rate target range at 3.75%–4%. Cook and Cleveland Fed President Hammack dissented in favor of a rate increase. In a speech in Santiago at 12:15 p.m. Eastern Time on November 20, Cook said that financing conditions remained accommodative, investment in artificial intelligence infrastructure continued to expand, and equity valuations were supporting household consumption. In her view, if demand continues to grow faster than the economy’s capacity to supply it, prices could face further upward pressure even with interest rates held steady. Based on the data available at the time, Cook estimated that the U.S. personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index rose 3.8% year over year in October, while the core PCE price index, which excludes food and energy, rose 3.2%. The price increases she observed extended across a range of goods and services, from airfares and hotel accommodation to appliances and furniture. Meanwhile, nonfarm payrolls increased by 165,000 in October, and the unemployment rate was 4.1%. The labor market’s resilience led her to view price stability as the more urgent priority at this stage. She worried that waiting until businesses and workers had incorporated higher inflation into prices and wages could require larger rate increases later. ... The University of Michigan’s final November survey, released the same day and based on interviews conducted from October 20 through November 16, showed that respondents’ median inflation expectation for the year ahead fell from 4.7% in October to 3.7%, while long-term inflation expectations declined from 3.5% to 3.3%. The survey’s research team noted that falling gasoline prices had eased financial pressure on some households with lower wealth. The sharp decline in near-term inflation expectations gives policymakers concerned about a persistent upward shift in expectations a reason to pause. Whether the relief from lower oil prices will extend to service prices, such as dining and accommodation, remains to be seen.

items.title: Democrats won big in the midterms. So now what? By Reuters
items.excerpt: WASHINGTON, Nov 21 (Reuters) - Democrats basking in their November 3 election wins will soon unveil an ambitious legislative agenda for the first 100 days and beyond, in a test of progressives’ influence and Republicans’ willingness to cooperate, as they take control of the US Congress on January 3. That agenda is likely to be unveiled in early December once a Senate leadership race is settled. It will mark a thunderous reversal of the past two years, when President Donald Trump’s Republicans ruled the Senate and House of Representatives. With their narrow majorities, they rammed through major tax cuts skewed toward the rich and stood by as Trump grabbed their powers over tariffs and spending. Democrats’ new majorities in Congress are anything but narrow. With a 56-44 majority in the Senate they are four votes short of the 60 votes needed to advance most legislation. In the House, their 257-172 force could grow beyond an 85-vote margin once a handful of races are settled. "This is a realignment," said Democratic Senator Raphael Warnock of Georgia in a post-election interview with reporters. But in a warning to Democrats, veteran Republican Senator John Boozman of Arkansas said in an interview that despite his party’s losses across the United States, Trump remains "a powerful force" and "I don’t see any of his vetoes getting overridden" by Congress during his remaining two years in office. AGGRESSIVE AGENDA For months, Democrats have been plotting a House-Senate coordinated attack to undo Trump’s major accomplishments, according to lawmakers and aides. With the high cost of living the top concern voiced by voters, Democratic leaders are going after the low-hanging fruit that also would help unite their party’s progressives and moderates. Early votes are expected on legislation handcuffing Trump’s ability to wage war on Iran without Congress’ approval, which would help lower gasoline prices. Reversing Republicans’ deep cuts to Medicaid and SNAP food stamp programs would begin helping the poor meet healthcare and grocery costs. Meanwhile, progressives have urged raising the federal minimum wage, which is unchanged since 2009 at $7.25 per hour. Some are pushing for $20 to $25. And in response to voter disgust over Washington ethics breaches, one of the first bills Democrats are expected to present is one barring lawmakers from insider trading of stocks. Republicans face a bind: joining Democrats could anger Trump unless he backs measures, while stonewalling could anger voters.

items.title: 2026 MAMA Awards Winners List: BTS & ENHYPEN Lead
items.excerpt: BTS, ENHYPEN, BIGBANG and CORTIS were the big winners of the 2026 MAMA Awards, which were held Friday and Saturday (Nov. 20-21) at the Kyocera Dome Osaka, in Japan. The awards streamed live worldwide on CJ ENM’s Mnet Plus platform. BTS won artist of the year, best male group and album of the year for ARIRANG. They also ranked in the top 10 for fans’ choice male and song of the year for “SWIM.” ENHYPEN won fans’ choice of the year, favorite MCD Stage and also ranked in the top 10 for fans’ choice male. Both groups have topped the all-genre Billboard 200 album chart this year. BTS led for three weeks in April with ARIRANG. ENHYPEN was on top for one week in September with The Sin: Bliss. BIGBANG won music visionary of the year and best music video, and also ranked in the top 10 for fans’ choice male. Taeyang of BIGBANG also won best dance performance male solo with “LIVE FAST DIE SLOW.” CORTIS won song of the year and best dance performance male group with “REDRED.” CORTIS also ranked in the top 10 for fans’ choice male. Yeonjun of TOMORROW X TOGETHER won best male artist. The group also made the top 10 for fans’ choice male. Soyeon of i-dle won best female artist. That group also made the top 10 for fans’ choice female. ALPHA DRIVE ONE and TUIDE were co-winners for best new artist. Music released between Oct. 1, 2025, and Sept. 30, 2026 was eligible for this year’s awards.
